skill.name: code-review-preferences
skill.description: Use this skill to review code and pull requests with a structured method, team standards, and concise feedback.
skill.summary: Applies a three-pass review method for practical, respectful code review feedback.
skill.author: ChaiWithJai

security_audit.summary: The two static network reconnaissance findings are false positives. Both point to normal review checklist headings and questions in SKILL.md, with no network activity, commands, scripts, or exfiltration intent found.

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 26-30 describe the correctness pass for code review, including bugs, edge cases, and security issues. There is no network reconnaissance instruction or operational behavior.
Lines 39-43 are a checklist for tests, bugs, security vulnerabilities, and secrets. The text is defensive review guidance, not reconnaissance or network access.

content.value_statement: Code reviews can become inconsistent and too subjective. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured method for focused review feedback.
actual_capabilities: Guides reviews through understand, correctness, and improvement passes.
Prioritizes bugs, edge cases, security issues, and secrets checks.
Encourages concise review feedback with a limit of five comments.
Promotes specific questions and line-focused suggestions.
Separates must-check, should-check, and nice-to-check review concerns.
limitations: Does not run tests, linters, or security scanners by itself.
Requires the user to provide code, a diff, or PR context.
Does not replace project-specific architecture or compliance review.
May need extra guidance for specialized languages or frameworks.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Apply a repeatable checklist before approving or requesting changes.

use_cases.title: Coach Junior Reviewers
use_cases.description: Teach reviewers to focus on correctness, clarity, and actionable feedback.

use_cases.title: Discuss Quality Standards
use_cases.description: Align a team around practical code review expectations and comment style.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change using the code-review-preferences skill. Focus on bugs, edge cases, and clear feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Pull Request Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the three-pass method on this PR. Identify must-fix issues first, then suggest up to five improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Security-Focused Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Check a change with security concerns
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change for correctness and security. Pay special attention to secrets, validation, authorization, and unsafe edge cases.

prompt_templates.title: Team Standards Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this diff against our team standards. Separate blocking issues from suggestions, and explain each comment with specific evidence.

output_examples.input: A user asks for review of a small bug fix.
output_examples.output: The review starts by restating the change goal, then flags one edge case and one missing test.

output_examples.input: A team lead asks for feedback on a pull request.
output_examples.output: The response groups comments by must-fix and suggested improvements, with no more than five total comments.

output_examples.input: A developer asks whether a refactor is ready to merge.
output_examples.output: The review checks behavior preservation, readability, test coverage, and consistency with existing patterns.

best_practices: Provide the diff, affected files, and the purpose of the change.
Ask for the review focus when security, performance, or compatibility matters.
Use the output as review guidance, then verify with tests and project owners.
anti_patterns: Using the skill to enforce personal style preferences without team agreement.
Requesting broad review without sharing enough code or context.
Treating suggested comments as a replacement for test execution.

faq.question: Does this skill run code or tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and feedback structure, but it does not execute commands.

faq.question: Can it review security issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It prompts reviewers to check for vulnerabilities and secrets, but it is not a security scanner.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What input should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide a diff, pasted code, file references, and the reason for the change.

faq.question: Will it comment on every issue?
faq.answer: No. It encourages a focused review with the most important comments first.

faq.question: Is it suitable for team standards?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps teams apply consistent review priorities and feedback style.
